name: Crashes and stuck turns found by the v0.1.9 bughunt (PR 1 of 3)
description: The crash and hang tier of the rusti-bughunt-s1 report. F1: a one-line draft longer than the input row crashed the TUI and lost the draft when the scrolled window started on a multi-byte char (an em dash, a curly quote, Cyrillic); input_window now drops that char as a char. F2: two byte-index cuts panicked the agent thread, on a provider error body that is not ASCII (llm::truncate) and on long non-ASCII background-job output (job_output, F4, whose panic also poisoned JOBS for the session); both cut on char boundaries now. With no panic net, a dead agent thread left the TUI on 'working…', RPC busy for the rest of the session and --json without a task_end; run_agent (and manual compaction in the TUI and RPC) now runs through ai_core::unpanic, so a panic comes back as the turn's error. F3: run_command, !cmd and hooks waited for EOF on pipes that a backgrounded child (`server &`) holds open, past the timeout, Esc and quit; the readers' bytes now collect in a buffer that is taken 500 ms after the shell exits, and Esc reaches a running command (a per-call flag relayed from the turn's cancel into the blocking pool, and the TUI's flag for !cmd). F11: a timed-out or interrupted command, a timed-out hook and job_stop now kill the whole tree: a process group on Unix, a job object on Windows. F9: --tui with no terminal on stdin exits 1 with the reason (the plain-stream fallback, which never started a task, is gone). F10: --rpc and --json never prompt on stdin: no saved model exits 1 with how to give one, and --tree and --json --resume without a task are refused.
evidence: Reproduced first in the rusti-bughunt-s1 scout (data/rusti-bughunt-s1/report.md, repros BH1-BH4, BH10, BH11), then as regression tests that fail on master: tests/rpc.rs a_provider_error_that_is_not_ascii_still_ends_the_turn, abort_kills_a_running_command, tui_without_a_terminal_exits_with_a_reason and rpc_and_json_without_a_model_exit_instead_of_asking, all four FAILED on 98b195f; unit tests tui::render a_long_draft_scrolls_from_any_char, llm an_error_body_is_cut_on_a_char_boundary, tools job_output_cuts_a_long_tail_on_a_char_boundary, a_backgrounded_child_does_not_hold_run_command and timeout_and_interrupt_kill_the_whole_command, hooks a_hook_that_backgrounds_a_child_answers_at_once, each FAILED with its fix reverted and passes with it; ai_core a_panic_in_a_turn_becomes_its_error. ./init.sh passes: cargo test 125 unit + 10 rpc + 1 trust. cargo clippy --all-targets adds no warnings. Built and tested on Windows with Git Bash only; the Unix process-group kill (own_group, Tree::kill) is not exercised here and is first run by the release workflow's cargo test on Linux and macOS.
decisions: The panic net is inside run_agent rather than at each front end's call, so the TUI, RPC, --json, one-shot runs and a delegate's sub-run all get it; a panicking sub-run fails its delegate call instead of the whole turn.

On Windows a command's tree is a job object, not taskkill /T: an MSYS exec under Git Bash leaves a Windows parent chain taskkill cannot follow (harness/memory/msys-exec-escapes-taskkill-tree.md). Closing the job kills nothing, so background jobs still outlive rusti as before.

On Unix every command, background job and hook runs in its own process group, killed as -pgid only while the shell is still unreaped, so a reused pid is never hit. Trade-off: Ctrl+C in a one-shot terminal run no longer reaches a running command's group.
Hooks get the bounded read and the tree kill at their timeout but no Esc: threading cancel through every hook event would touch every caller, and the timeout (default 30 s) now holds.
After the shell exits the readers get 500 ms; the result then notes that a background process still holds the output and points at run_background.
Not in this PR (other workers, PRs 2 and 3): F5 widths, F6 CRLF edits, F7 cmd /C, F8 /mcp freeze, F12 cargo-install reload, F13 colours, F14 noise, F15 picker label.
